captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 4. In this lesson: Read all about it!
Find the five Ws (who, what, where, when, why) in a news report.
Here are some new words. Headline. The title of a news story, in big letters. Reporter.
A person who writes news stories. Event. Something important that happens.
Listen and say them. headline
reporter
event.
And some more words. Witness. A person who saw something happen. Rescue.
Save someone from danger. Local. From the area near you. Listen and say them. witness
rescue
local.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: the title of a news story, in big letters?
Now some grammar: Past simple in reports.
News reports usually use the past simple because the event has already happened.
For example: A dog rescued a boy from the river. For example: Firefighters arrived at 3 p.m.
Now listen, and read along. Dog saves boy from river. Hero dog saves boy from river!
A brave dog called Bruno rescued a seven-year-old boy from the River Lane in Millbrook last Sunday afternoon.
Sam Tran fell into the water while he was playing near the bank.
His friend shouted for help.
Bruno, who belongs to a local farmer, jumped into the river and pulled Sam to the side.
‘I couldn't believe it,’ said one witness, Mrs Lopez.
‘The dog swam straight to him.’ Sam was cold and wet but not hurt.
Bruno is going to get a special medal next week.
Another question. The video will stop. Who is the hero of the report?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like headline, reporter, event.
You practised past simple in reports. And you read Dog saves boy from river.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 4. In this lesson: Writing a headline.
Write short headlines and use pronouns to avoid repetition.
Here are some new words. Short. Not long. Catchy. Easy to remember and interesting. Fact.
Something that is true. Listen and say them. short
catchy
fact.
And some more words. Opinion. What someone thinks or feels. Quote.
The exact words someone said. Article. A piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine.
Listen and say them. opinion
quote
article.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: not long?
Now some grammar: Pronouns. Pronouns (he, she, it, they, him, her,
them) take the place of nouns so we don't repeat words. For example: Mia won the race.
She was very happy. For example: The boys found a kitten and took it home.
Now listen, and read along. School garden wins prize. School garden grows into winner!
Pupils at Green Hill Primary School won first prize in the Town Garden Competition on Friday.
The children planted vegetables, flowers and two apple trees behind their school.
They worked on the garden every week for a year.
Head teacher Mr Ali said, ‘I am very proud of them.
They worked hard in the sun and in the rain.’
The school is going to use the prize money to build a small greenhouse.
Another question. The video will stop. Which school won the prize?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like short, catchy, fact. You practised pronouns.
And you read School garden wins prize. Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
